'''Andrea Bargnani''' ({{IPA|it|anˈdrɛːa barˈɲaːni}}; born 26 October 1985) is an Italian former professional [[basketball]] player. The {{Convert|7|ft|4=2|adj=on}} [[power forward]]-[[center (basketball)|center]]<ref name="stats">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andrea_bargnani/career_stats.html |title=Andrea Bargnani Info Page – Career Stats and Totals |work=NBA.com |access-date=20 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150128233616/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andrea_bargnani/career_stats.html |archive-date=28 January 2015 }}</ref> played for [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]] in the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]] and the [[EuroLeague]] before being selected first overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He spent 10 seasons in the NBA, including with the [[New York Knicks]] and [[Brooklyn Nets]], before ending his career with a stint in Spain during the 2016–17 season.

==Professional career==
===Stella Azzurra Roma (2002–2003)===
Bargnani began his basketball career in 2002–03 with [[Stella Azzurra Roma]] in the Italian fourth-tiered league [[Serie B Basket|Serie B2]], averaging 13.2 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 4.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in 23 games.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andrea_bargnani/bio.html |title=Andrea Bargnani Info Page – Bio |work=NBA.com |access-date=20 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130114222451/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andrea_bargnani/bio.html |archive-date=14 January 2013 }}</ref>

===Benetton Treviso (2003–2006)===
In 2003–04, Bargnani joined [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]] side [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]]. He posted averages of 4.2 points and 1.6 rebounds in 10 games.<ref name=eurostats>{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Andrea-Bargnani-154/stats|title=Bargnani Serie A & Euroleague stats|work=DraftExpress.com|access-date=23 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130131162540/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Andrea-Bargnani-154/stats/|archive-date=31 January 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made eight appearances in the [[EuroLeague]], recording 2.4 points and 1.5 rebounds per outing.<ref name=eurostats/> Incidentally, Bargnani faced his future team, the [[Toronto Raptors]], on 20 October 2003 in a pre-season game at [[Air Canada Centre]]. He tallied 13 points, five rebounds, one [[steal (basketball)|steal]] and two [[block (basketball)|blocks]] in 22 minutes in an 86–83 defeat to the Raptors.

In 2004–05, he averaged 6.8 points and 3.1 rebounds in 28 LBA games for Benetton, and averaged 3.7 points and 2.1 rebounds in 12 EuroLeague matches.<ref name=eurostats/>

In the 2005–06 LBA season, he averaged 12 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.3 blocks and 1.4 steals in 47 games for Benetton.<ref name=eurostats/> He posted a season high of 25 points against Rome. He shot .483 from the field and .399 from [[three-point range]], and led the LBA in blocks with 63. In the process, he helped lead Benetton to the 2006 LBA title. In the 2005–06 EuroLeague season, he contributed 10.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals, while shooting .508 percent from the floor and .434 from three-point range in 18 games.<ref name=eurostats/> He posted a season-high 20 points against [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] and [[SIG Strasbourg|Strasbourg]].<ref name=bio/> Bargnani was subsequently named the [[EuroLeague Rising Star]], the award given to each EuroLeague season's best EuroLeague player aged 22 or under, for the 2005–06 season.<ref name=bio/>

===Toronto Raptors (2006–2013)===
====2006–07 season====
[[File:Andrea Bargnani.JPG|thumb|upright|Bargnani with the Raptors in 2007]]
As a prospect, Bargnani drew many comparisons to German NBA player [[Dirk Nowitzki]], mainly due to his ability to shoot [[Three-point field goal|from the perimeter]], his mobility despite his size, and his ball-handling skills.<ref>{{cite web |last=Broussard |first=Chris |author-link=Chris Broussard |date=28 February 2007 |title=ESPN The Magazine: Meet Andrea Bargnani |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?page=espnmag/bargnani |access-date=28 February 2007 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Kevin |last=Pelton |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/preview070311.html |title=Insider Preview – Sonics at Toronto |work=NBA.com |date=11 March 2007 |access-date=11 March 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090220152415/http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/preview070311.html |archive-date=20 February 2009 }}</ref> Bargnani entered the [[2006 NBA draft]] and was selected first overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Schuhmann|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2006/numberone_060628.html|title=The Long Journey for No. 1|work=NBA.com|date=28 June 2006|access-date=28 June 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090620005838/http://www.nba.com/draft2006/numberone_060628.html|archive-date=20 June 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is the first European player,<ref name=bio/> sixth non-American player, and second player without [[college basketball|U.S. college]] or [[high school]] experience to be drafted first overall, after [[Yao Ming]].

Bargnani made his regular-season debut against the [[New Jersey Nets]] on 1 November 2006, posting 2 points, 2 rebounds and 2 blocks in eight minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nets 102-92 Raptors (2 Nov, 2006) Box Score - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/261101017 |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=ESPN}}</ref> In the process, he also became the fourth-ever Italian-born player to play in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web |last=Robbins |first=Liz |date=28 June 2006 |title=Going Where No Italian Has Gone |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/06/28/sports/basketball/28nba.html |access-date=28 June 2006 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Like many rookies, Bargnani took some time to adapt to the league and as he slowly improved his game, his confidence and playing time increased. In turn, the home fans soon warmed up to Bargnani; on 7 January 2007, ten thousand Bargnani figurines were given away at [[Air Canada Centre]] for the game against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/postup_010707.html |title=Raptors Post-Up |work=NBA.com |date=7 January 2007 |access-date=7 January 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090103071320/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/postup_010707.html |archive-date=3 January 2009 }}</ref> As the mid-season approached, Bargnani was selected as NBA's [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] Rookie of the Month (January 2007),<ref name="rotm">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/bargnani_020107.html |title=Bargnani Named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month |work=NBA.com |date=1 February 2007 |access-date=1 February 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081201065114/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/bargnani_020107.html |archive-date=1 December 2008 }}</ref> joining teammate [[Jorge Garbajosa]] (winner of the award in December 2006) as the sixth Raptors player to win the monthly honour.<ref name="rotm"/> Together with Garbajosa, Bargnani was also selected to play in the [[2007 NBA All-Star Game|T-Mobile Rookie Challenge game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/allstar2007/news/challenge_070131.html|title=No. 1 Draft Picks Bargnani and Bogut Head Selections For 2007 T-Mobile Rookie Challenge & Youth Jam|work=NBA.com|date=31 January 2007|access-date=31 January 2007}}</ref> After the [[NBA All-Star weekend|All-Star break]], Bargnani continued to work on his defence and shooting (averaging 14.3 points per game (ppg) and 3.9 rebounds per game (rpg) in 12 games in February 2007), and he was selected as the Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for the second straight time on 1 March 2007.<ref name=rotm2>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/pr_bargnani030107.html |title=Bargnani Named NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month |work=NBA.com |date=1 March 2007 |access-date=1 March 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116010950/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/pr_bargnani030107.html |archive-date=16 January 2009 }}</ref> Bargnani became the third Raptor ever to win the award twice, joining [[Vince Carter]] and [[Damon Stoudamire]].<ref name=rotm2/>

On 21 March 2007, Bargnani underwent emergency [[appendectomy]] surgery after being taken to hospital following illness experienced after practice the night before.<ref>{{cite web |date=22 May 2007 |others=Contributed the Associated Press |title=Raptors' Bargnani has appendix removed |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2806697 |access-date=22 May 2007 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He recovered after about a month, and ended the season averaging 11.6 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.<ref name="stats"/> His performances were credited as helping the Raptors to their first-ever [[Atlantic Division (NBA)|Division]] title, as well as their first [[NBA playoffs]] berth in five years; Bargnani came in second for [[NBA Rookie of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2857872|title=Roy receives 127 of 128 first-place votes as top rookie|publisher=ESPN|date=3 May 2007|access-date=3 May 2007}}</ref> In the [[2007 NBA playoffs]], Bargnani averaged 11.0 ppg and 4.0 rpg as the Raptors were defeated by the [[New Jersey Nets]] 4–2 in the first round.<ref name=stats/> On 8 May 2007, Bargnani and Garbajosa were named to the NBA All-Rookie team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/all_rookie_2007s.html |title=Andrea Bargnani & Jorge Garbajosa Highlight 2007 All-Rookie Team |work=NBA.com |date=8 May 2007 |access-date=11 May 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115213354/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/all_rookie_2007s.html |archive-date=15 January 2009 }}</ref>

====2007–08 season====
On 5 October 2007, the Raptors announced they had exercised a third-year option on Bargnani, giving a guaranteed NBA contract through the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]] and retaining a fourth-year option for the [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/bargnani_100507.html |title=Raptors Exercise Third Year Option on Andrea Bargnani |work=NBA.com |date=5 October 2007 |access-date=5 October 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115094113/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/bargnani_100507.html |archive-date=15 January 2009 }}</ref> Prior to the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], Bargnani was voted by the general managers of the league as the "international player most likely to have a breakout season".<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Grange|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/raptors/2007/10/25/gms_tip_bargnani_for_big_year.html|title=GMs tip Bargnani for big year|work=TheStar.com|date=25 October 2007|access-date=26 October 2007|archive-date=19 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130619203914/http://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/raptors/2007/10/25/gms_tip_bargnani_for_big_year.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was selected to play with the Sophomores in the T-Mobile Rookie Challenge during the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/moonbargnani_013008.html |title=Bargnani & Moon Selected To Play In '08 T-Mobile Rookie Challenge |work=NBA.com |date=30 January 2008 |access-date=30 January 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081201171321/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/moonbargnani_013008.html |archive-date=1 December 2008 }}</ref> Bargnani was widely criticised for having a poor season. His statistics had gone down, he was not grabbing enough rebounds, was unable to shoot well, got into foul trouble easily and did not drive to the basket enough.<ref name=stats/><ref name=off>{{cite web|first=Dave|last=Feschuk|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/raptors/2008/04/30/raptors_bargnani_a_symbol_of_stalled_progress.html|title=Raptors' Bargnani a symbol of stalled progress|work=TheStar.com|date=30 April 2008|access-date=30 April 2008}}</ref> He did not feature prominently in the [[2008 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] either—in which the Raptors were eliminated by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the first round—and there were even calls for him to be traded.<ref name=off/>

====2008–09 season====
[[File:raptors v magic 2009 bargnani.jpg|thumb|upright|Bargnani averaged 15.4 points and 1.3 blocks per game in the second half of the 2008–09 season.]]
However, Toronto did not give up on Bargnani yet and committed the entire summer coaching him to become a more effective interior player, forcing him to drive to the basket more and settle less for jump shots. The arrival of six-time [[NBA All-Star]] [[Jermaine O'Neal]] also meant that Bargnani was likely to come off the bench in most games, with Bosh and O'Neal forming the starting [[frontcourt]]. During the summer he worked hard on his body, putting up some more weight (adding some {{convert|15|lb|0|disp=sqbr}} of muscle); this work showed his effects in the first games of the regular campaign, when he was more willing to rebound in traffic and drive to the basket.<ref name=musc>{{cite web|first=Doug|last=Smith|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/raptors/2008/11/16/bargnani_could_shift_to_raptors_starting_unit.html|title=Bargnani could shift to Raptors' starting unit|work=TheStar.com|date=16 November 2008|access-date=16 November 2008}}</ref> He also seemed to rediscover his shooting stroke, had better shot selection and became a consistent shot-blocker, and he was soon moved to the starting line-up as [[small forward]].<ref name=musc/>

On 21 November 2008, Bargnani recorded a career-high 29 points, as well as 10 rebounds in an [[overtime (sport)|overtime]] loss against New Jersey.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/recap_112108.html |title=Big Night From Bosh, Bargnani, Calderon Not Enough |work=NBA.com |date=21 November 2008 |access-date=22 November 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090302143751/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/recap_112108.html |archive-date=2 March 2009 }}</ref> After some stumbles in December, he hit good form in January, averaging 21.2 points and 6.7 rebounds over a 15-game stretch as he became the starting center in place for the injured O'Neal,<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Grange|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/oneal-indifferent-to-trade-talk/article20443150/|title=O'Neal indifferent to trade talk|work=TheGlobeAndMail.com|date=16 January 2009|access-date=16 January 2009}}</ref> recording a career-high 31 points against Chicago in the process.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290114028|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090119074555/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290114028|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 January 2009|title=Rose's 4th-quarter run, Deng's return to starting lineup carry Bulls|publisher=ESPN|date=14 January 2009|access-date=14 January 2009}}</ref> O'Neal was then traded to [[Miami Heat|Miami]] during the All-Star break,<ref>{{cite web|first=David|last=Aldridge|url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/features/david_aldridge/02/13/heatraptorstrade.20090213/index.html|title=Raptors trade O'Neal, Moon to Heat for Marion, Banks|work=NBA.com|date=13 February 2009|access-date=13 February 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090215212758/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/features/david_aldridge/02/13/heatraptorstrade.20090213/index.html|archive-date=15 February 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> allowing the Italian to regain his starting spot for the rest of the season. He averaged 19.8, 17.9 and 20.3 points per game for January, February and March, respectively,<ref name="espnlog">{{cite web |title=Andrea Bargnani Game Log - 2015-16 Regular Season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2987/type/nba/year/2016 |access-date=26 September 2024 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> even as Toronto went on several losing streaks and gradually fell out of the playoff race. The Raptors concluded the regular season with 33 wins, and ranked 13th in the Eastern Conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2009.html|title=2008-09 NBA Season Summary|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=16 April 2009}}</ref> Meanwhile, Bargnani recorded career-high averages in points per game, field goal percentage, three-point percentage, rebounds and blocks.<ref name=stats/> On 8 July 2009, he signed a contract extension with the Raptors that paid him US$50 million over five seasons, starting in 2010–11.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2009/07/08/report_raptors_sign_bargnani_for_5_years.html|title=Report: Raptors sign Bargnani for 5 years|work=TheStar.com|date=8 July 2009|access-date=8 July 2009}}</ref>

====2009–10 season====
[[File:Andrea bargnani dunk 2009 2.JPG|thumb|left|Bargnani going in for a dunk in a game against [[Miami Heat|Miami]], 20 November 2009]]
Bargnani's form and numbers continued in the [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]]. In the first ten games, the center averaged 19.3 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game; by mid-season, he had seven [[double-double]]s, a career high.<ref name=espnlog/> Toronto struggled at the start of the season, going as low as six games below .500, but reached the mid-point with a 21–20 record. On 2 February 2010, Bargnani scored a career-high 34 points in a loss against the [[Indiana Pacers]]; he later scored 33 in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Although Toronto were six games above .500 at one point, their form spiralled downwards after the All-Star break. Coupled with two separate injuries to [[Chris Bosh]], Toronto slid from the fifth seed to the eighth, and were subsequently locked in a race with [[Chicago Bulls|Chicago]] for the final spot. That spot was only decided on the final day, when Chicago won their last game and ended the season 41–41, one game ahead of Toronto. On Bargnani's part, he averaged career highs in points, rebounds, blocks and minutes.

====2010–11 season====
Toronto's franchise player [[Chris Bosh]] opted to leave for [[Miami Heat|Miami]] as a [[free agent]] after his contract with the Raptors was up. As a result, Bargnani became the focal point of Toronto's offense. On 8 December 2010, he scored a career-high 41 points in a losing effort against the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301208018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101212232849/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301208018|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 December 2010|title=Raymond Felton hits tiebreaking 3 as Knicks beat Raptors|publisher=ESPN|date=9 December 2010|access-date=9 December 2010}}</ref> Bargnani had a career year, averaging 21 points, 5 rebounds and 1 block.

====2011–12 season====
During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Bargnani chose not to sign overseas and decided instead to work on his game and develop into more of a power forward following the Raptors' acquisition of Lithuanian center [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Konstantinos|last=Charitopoulos|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/821955-why-nba-lockout-doesnt-harm-andrea-bargnani-at-least-now|title=Why NBA Lockout Doesn't Harm Andrea Bargnani, at Least Now.|work=BleacherReport.com|date=26 August 2011|access-date=26 August 2011}}</ref> On 28 March 2012, in a game against the Denver Nuggets, Bargnani scored 26 points and became the fourth player to ever score 6,000 points as a Raptor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 March 2012 |others=The Associated Press |title=Bargnani, Raptors dispatch Nuggets |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/bargnani-raptors-dispatch-nuggets-1.1154227 |access-date=26 September 2024 |website=cbc.ca}}</ref>

====2012–13 season====
After managing the first 21 games of the season, Bargnani missed the next two months of action with the Raptors following an elbow injury in early December.<ref>{{cite web|first=Russell|last=Steinberg|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2012/12/12/3761098/andrea-bargnani-injury-raptors|title=Andrea Bargnani injury: Raptors big man has torn ligaments in elbow|work=SBNation.com|date=12 December 2012|access-date=12 December 2012}}</ref> He returned to the line-up on 6 February 2013, but after managing another 14 games, he was ruled out for the rest of the season on 13 March because of the same injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/andrea-bargnani-injury-update-2/ |title=Andrea Bargnani Injury Update |work=Raptors.com |date=13 March 2013 |access-date=13 March 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141011012002/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/andrea-bargnani-injury-update-2/ |archive-date=11 October 2014 }}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2013–2015)===

====2013–14 season====
On 10 July 2013, Bargnani was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Steve Novak]], [[Marcus Camby]] and [[Quentin Richardson]], along with a future first-round draft pick ([[2016 NBA draft|2016]]) and two future second-round draft picks ([[2014 NBA draft|2014]] and [[2017 NBA draft|2017]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/nyktrade_071013/ |title=Raptors Acquire Three Players, Three Picks From Knicks |work=NBA.com |date=10 July 2013 |access-date=10 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006152814/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/nyktrade_071013/ |archive-date=6 October 2014 }}</ref>

On 18 December 2013, in a game at the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], with 20 seconds remaining in overtime in which the Knicks held a two-point lead, Bargnani received an offensive rebound and shot a three-pointer that missed (instead of dribbling out the clock or getting fouled to go to the free throw line). The game went into double-overtime as a result, where the Knicks fortunately outscored the Bucks 13–7 to hold on for a 107–101 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cox |first=Zack |date=2013-12-19 |title=Andrea Bargnani Says Ill-Advised Overtime Shot Was 'Aggressive,' 'Definitely a Mistake' |url=https://nesn.com/2013/12/andrea-bargnani-says-ill-advised-overtime-shot-was-aggressive-definitely-a-mistake/ |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=NESN.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 22 January 2014, in a loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Bargnani suffered a torn ligament in his left elbow after a failed dunk attempt, and was ruled out indefinitely, eventually missing the rest of the regular season.<ref name="j953">{{cite web | last=Youngmisuk | first=Ohm | title=Knicks' Bargnani out with torn elbow ligament | website=ESPN.com | date=2014-01-23 | url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/10341003/new-york-knicks-andrea-bargnani-torn-elbow-ligament | access-date=2024-12-02}}</ref> The Knicks finished the season at 37–45 and missed the playoffs.

====2014–15 season====
After missing most of the preseason with a hamstring injury, Bargnani was set to make his season debut on 22 November when he was ruled out indefinitely again with a strained calf muscle.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sean|last=Highkin|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2014/11/23/andrea-bargnani-out-indefinitely-after-suffering-calf-strain/|title=Andrea Bargnani out indefinitely after suffering calf strain|work=NBCSports.com|date=23 November 2014|access-date=23 November 2014}}</ref> He went on to make his season debut on 31 December against the Los Angeles Clippers after having not played for nearly a year. In just under 20 minutes of action off the bench, he recorded 9 points, 4 rebounds and 2 assists in the 78–99 loss.<ref>{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Berman|url=https://nypost.com/2015/01/01/knicks-bargnani-shows-some-positive-signs-in-season-debut/|title=How Andrea Bargnani fared in much-delayed season debut|work=NYPost.com|date=1 January 2015|access-date=1 January 2015}}</ref> However, the following game on 2 January, Bargnani re-injured his right calf during the first quarter of the Knicks' 81–97 loss to the Detroit Pistons.<ref>{{cite web |last=Schonbrun |first=Zach |date=2 January 2015 |title=Knicks, Desperate for Points and Bodies, Fall Again |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/01/03/sports/basketball/knicks-desperate-for-points-and-bodies-fall-again.html |access-date=26 September 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> He missed a further 16 games before making his second return of the season against Miami on 9 February.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrea Bargnani Game Log - 2014-15 Regular Season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2987/type/nba/year/2015 |access-date=26 September 2024 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2015–2016)===
On 17 July 2015, Bargnani signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sapp |first=Demetris |date=17 July 2015 |title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN ANDREA BARGNANI |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-sign-andrea-bargnani |access-date=23 September 2024 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the Nets in the team's season opener against the Chicago Bulls on 28 October, recording 17 points and 7 rebounds off the bench in a 115–100 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/CHIBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Bulls beat Nets 115-100 for 2-0 start|work=NBA.com|date=28 October 2015|access-date=28 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124043047/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/CHIBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=24 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 10 December, he scored a season-high 23 points in a 110–91 win over the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151210/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Bargnani scores season-best 23, Nets beat 76ers 100-91|work=NBA.com|date=10 December 2015|access-date=10 December 2015}}</ref> On 20 February 2016, he was waived by the Nets.<ref>{{cite web |date=20 February 2016 |title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Andrea Bargnani |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/02/20/brooklyn-nets-waive-andrea-bargnani |access-date=23 September 2024 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Baskonia (2016–2017)===
On 26 July 2016, Bargnani returned to Europe and signed a two-year deal with Spanish club [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]].<ref>{{cite news |date=26 July 2016 |title=Andrea Bargnani 2006 NBA Draft first pick is Laboral Kutxa Baskonia new player |url=https://www.baskonia.com/en/andrea-bargnani-2006-nba-draft-first-pick-is-laboral-kutxa-baskonia-new-player/ |access-date=23 September 2024 |work=baskonia.com}}</ref> On 14 October 2016, in his first [[EuroLeague]] game of the season, Bargnani scored a season-best 26 points in an 85–84 win over [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]].<ref>{{cite web |date=14 October 2016 |title=Baskonia Vitoria Gasteiz vs Anadolu Efes Istanbul |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/?gamecode=6&seasoncode=E2016#!boxscore |access-date=26 September 2024 |publisher=EuroLeague}}</ref> On 26 April 2017, Baskonia parted ways with Bargnani after a plague of injuries.<ref>{{cite news |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=26 April 2017 |title=Andrea Bargnani, Baskonia officially part ways |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/233048/andrea-bargnani-baskonia-officially-part-ways.html |access-date=26 September 2024 |work=sportando.com}}</ref> In 15 EuroLeague games, he averaged 8.8 points per game, and in 14 [[Liga ACB|ACB]] games, he averaged 11.5 points per game.

==National team career==
[[File:Andrea Bargnani (Italy).jpg|thumb|upright|Bargnani playing for the Italian national team]]
Bargnani played for the Italian junior and under-20 national teams. He competed on the World Select Team at the 2004 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. He also featured in [[EuroBasket 2007]], representing the [[Italy men's national basketball team|Italian senior national team]]. Italy finished ninth in the competition, and in six games, Bargnani averaged 12.7 points and 5.0 rebounds in 28.7 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket2007.org/en/cid_BqypGFJPHy-Nw4lwIAq,v3.teamID_307.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2007.roundID_5169.playerID_36246.html |title=Andrea Bargnani (Italy) |website=Eurobasket2007.org |access-date=30 September 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716181226/http://www.eurobasket2007.org/en/cid_BqypGFJPHy-Nw4lwIAq%2Cv3.teamID_307.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2007.roundID_5169.playerID_36246.html |archive-date=16 July 2010 }}</ref>

He was called up to the Italian squad that took part in [[EuroBasket 2015]].<ref>{{cite web |date=2 September 2015 |title=Italy take their dream roster to Berlin |url=https://www.fibaeurope.com/season_2015.coid_s,Z8kZaZIlsLwQFktgGes0.articleMode_on.html |access-date=26 September 2024 |website=FIBAEurope.com}}</ref> Bargnani averaged 14.8 points and 3.6 rebounds per game, while Italy finished the tournament in sixth place.

==Post-retirement==
In 2025, he was named LBA executive advisor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-15 |title=Where Are The Players From The Knicks’ 17-65 Season Now? - Fadeaway World |url=https://fadeawayworld.net/nba/new-york-knicks/where-are-the-players-from-the-knicks-17-65-season-now |access-date=2026-05-15 |language=en-US}}</ref>
